A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PSN/GIN research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable matching despite the changed title, extensive reformatting, and table reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original Monte Carlo prediction and planning experiments, including inferred-goal evaluation, transfer to 20 agents, and CITR pedestrian prediction in Tables 2–7.

after.justification: v3 retains original prediction and planning results across these scenarios in Tables 2–5 and the full planning tables in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The PSN/GIN architectures, continuous mask relaxation, training losses, threshold/rank selection, and receding-horizon procedures are retained. V3 clarifies that planning goals are inferred once at initialization, consistent with v2 Algorithm 2; this does not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions train in 4- and 10-agent scenarios and evaluate prediction/planning with known or inferred goals, 20-agent prediction, and CITR pedestrian prediction. Combining existing prediction tables does not add dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: V3 removes the full-player All comparator from inferred-goal prediction and CITR prediction, where it appeared in v2 Tables 5 and 7. All remains in planning comparisons. The seven selection baselines remain; changing Jacobian to Gradient in certain rows standardizes the name of the existing comparator.

E3.justification: The reported dynamics, horizons, training budgets, thresholds, metrics, and nearest-neighbor pre-filter for 20-agent evaluation are retained. V3's corrected explanation of selection consistency agrees with the formula already present in v2's appendix.

E4.justification: The threshold/rank visualization, Full/Partial comparisons, inferred-goal evaluation, and transfer analyses are retained. V3's discussion of limited temporal flicker interprets existing consistency scores; it introduces no additional robustness experiment or case study.

E5.justification: V3 Table 2 first reports maximum-across-method standard errors for the 20-agent and CITR blocks, absent from v2 Tables 6 and 7. Existing bootstrapped reporting is retained elsewhere. No increased run count or newly specified seeds are established.

E6.justification: Matched prediction and planning scores are unchanged, but three All prediction rows are removed, including inferred-goal ADE/FDE values of 0.2565/0.4284 and 0.4233/0.7078. V3 also corrects the CITR finding: PSN achieves the best ADE, while Distance achieves the best FDE, 0.4285.

T1.justification: The Nash and masked-game definitions, mathematical objectives, mask relaxation, dynamics, and appendix metric formulas are retained. Reformatting and explanatory corrections introduce no new theorem, proof, derivation, or substantive formal assumption.

C1.justification: V3 qualifies v2's outperformance and state-of-the-art claims as competitive or often better performance against evaluated explicit selection baselines. Contribution iv retains the 50–75% game-size reduction but drops the claim of a vast runtime speedup. The central PSN/GIN contributions remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V3 limits the generalization inference to the tested 10-to-20-agent transfer with candidate pre-filtering, replacing v2's broader suggestion that different agent counts need no retraining. It also replaces the CITR inference about human attention with a dataset-specific prediction interpretation and adds discussion of temporal stability and benchmark limitations.

D1.justification: Network architecture, training-data generation, hyperparameters, scenario specifications, and cited solver access information are retained in Appendix A. The relocated baseline definitions repeat v2 Section 4.1.3 rather than disclose new implementation information.

R1.justification: Sections 2.1–2.2 add Khan et al. (2026), Liu et al. (2024a), Qiu et al. (2026), and Vakil and Pierson (2026), emphasizing hierarchical interactions, formation, and swarms. Schwarting et al. (2021) and Wang et al. (2021) are removed with the racing discussion. This is a localized positioning update.

P1.justification: V3 retitles the paper and extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, experimental discussion, and conclusion. It clarifies variant terminology and pseudocode, moves baseline definitions into Appendix A.2, reorders the adaptation subsections, and restructures the appendices.

P2.justification: V3 changes the document from two-column to single-column presentation, merges v2 Tables 2, 6, and 7 into Table 2, and presents compact planning tables with full versions rotated in Appendix C. Figures and algorithms are resized and relocated. These are substantial display changes, while the three figures retain their underlying content.

improvement.justification: V3 improves claim calibration, corrects the CITR winner, adds uncertainty reporting, and resolves crowded table presentation. However, removing full-player prediction references weakens assessment of the accuracy–computation tradeoff, especially where those references outperform selection methods. The CITR discussion also retains a full-player comparison without its numerical row. These benefits and losses prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
